question: Should OpenClaw core add native cross-gateway session messaging now, or keep gateway-to-gateway messaging outside core until a federation trust contract is approved?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but the implementation shape changes gateway trust boundaries, session ownership, message delivery guarantees, and core-vs-plugin responsibility.

options.title: Design core federation contract first
options.body: Define peer identity, authorization scopes, replay/idempotency, session visibility, and upgrade behavior before landing a core implementation.

options.title: Keep it as plugin or bridge work
options.body: Leave core session tools gateway-local and add only the missing plugin/API seams needed for safe external bridges.

options.title: Wait for the broad FRD
options.body: Hold this issue behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 until maintainers settle the federation protocol and tenant-scoped operator policy.

recommendation.title: Design core federation contract first
recommendation.body: Define peer identity, authorization scopes, replay/idempotency, session visibility, and upgrade behavior before landing a core implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail spans the session tool architecture and gateway URL security boundary that this decision would change.
